source_snapshot.procedure: Create mdadm level [0|1|5] with four named NVMe members, format/mount/copy/hash, fail/remove/re-add one member, wait for rebuild, recheck hash and tear down.
source_snapshot.criteria: Create, fault, remove, add and rebuild successfully with correct file hash and array state.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL supplies a guessed two-device /dev/md0 workflow and omits the source fault/rebuild lifecycle.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Requires confirmation of RAID1, four-member topology, exact disposable targets and complete destructive lifecycle.

old_problem: The RAID1 title coexisted with a generic level placeholder, and DeepSeek changed the explicit four-device /dev/md3 source topology to an unsupported guessed two-device /dev/md0 shortcut.
disposition_reason: The row title fixes level=1 and the Procedure explicitly supplies four members and /dev/md3; a four-way Linux md RAID1 is valid. Stable identities replace volatile names at runtime without reducing member count. Full one-member fail/remove/re-add/rebuild, file integrity and teardown coverage remains destructive and separately authorized.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row131 all18 XLSX cells and history2738.
Interpreted the placeholder as level=1 from the row identity while preserving the explicit four-member topology and /dev/md3 role.
Restored the complete fault/rebuild/hash/teardown lifecycle and rejected DeepSeek's two-device shortcut; no storage or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Parameterized four-member mdadm RAID1 fault, rebuild, integrity and teardown validation
test_case.purpose: Verify an approved disposable four-way NVMe mdadm RAID1 sustains one member fault/removal, rebuilds after that exact member is re-added, preserves the 512 MiB file, and tears down cleanly.
required_package: Critical destructive authorization and proof all members are non-boot, unmounted, non-swap, non-LVM, non-RAID and data-free
Approved 512 MiB source file/hash, mount path, rebuild timeout/health thresholds
Exact one-member fault/re-add plan, OOB access, abort criteria and teardown/recovery
test_case.test_command: After stable-identity exclusions and explicit approval, create /dev/md3 as level=1 with exactly four approved members, verify all active sync, mkfs/mount and copy/hash the 512 MiB file. Fail and remove exactly one mapped member, prove degraded service, re-add the same approved member, monitor recovery to all active sync, recheck the destination hash, then cleanly unmount/stop and zero metadata only on those four members.
test_case.expected_result: The four-member RAID1 reaches healthy active-sync state, remains available and hash-correct with exactly one member failed/removed, rebuilds that member to healthy, preserves file integrity, and is precisely dismantled without other device impact.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires four exact members, level=1 state transitions, single-member degraded availability, observed rebuild progress/completion, matching pre/post destination hash and clean targeted teardown. A two-device shortcut does not satisfy this row.
safety_gate: Destructive approval precedes create, mkfs, member fault and zero-superblock.
Protect OS/boot/EFI, mounted, swap, LVM/device-mapper, existing RAID, management and valuable-data devices by stable identity.
Fault only one recorded member and never introduce a second fault while degraded or rebuilding.
Abort on identity drift, unexpected array/signature, filesystem error, stalled rebuild, media/thermal/power/BMC fault or failed unmount; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Preflight exclusions and exact create/detail active-sync baseline
Fail/remove/degraded, re-add and timestamped rebuild progress/completion
Post-rebuild hash, unmount/stop/targeted cleanup, final topology and logs
test_case.recovery: If fault/rebuild deviates, stop new mutations, keep the remaining three members untouched, preserve mdadm detail/events/health/log evidence and require the storage owner to select recovery. Never fail another member or clear metadata until the array is safely unmounted and teardown is explicitly approved.
